html:
The Stillaguamish are a Coast Salish people of the Stillaguamish River valley in northwest Washington, north of today's Everett. They speak Lushootseed, like their neighbours the Snohomish and Skagit.

They lived in villages of cedar plank houses along the river and depended on its salmon runs. In 1855 they were included in the Treaty of Point Elliott, which gave most of the Puget Sound lands to the United States. Not wanting to leave their river, many stayed on scattered homesteads instead of moving to the Tulalip reservation. As a result their tribe gained federal recognition only in 1976.
